title: signed Mirror expert mixture
hypothesis: A signed mixture of four Givens-coordinate views of one shared expert matrix can reproduce an aligned four-expert mixture teacher at lower actual serialized payload than independent signed full experts; independently parameterized mixture experts should require private degrees of freedom.
physical_object: one shared linear expert matrix W mapping 16D inputs to 12D outputs
mirror_coordinate: four expert-specific Givens coordinate vectors on the input representation
logical_multiplicity: four signed-mixture expert functions evaluated jointly per example

task.mixture: coefficients are (+/- 0.5) Walsh sign patterns from signs of x[0] and x[1]; all four experts are composed for every example

teacher_modes.aligned_views: one random base matrix W with four fixed Givens input views

task.structure_audit: maximum per-sign-pattern MSE across four coefficient patterns

controls: independent full expert matrices with the same signed coefficients
hard tied expert matrix with the same signed coefficients
shared matrix with learned per-expert scalar amplitudes
shared matrix plus rank-1 per-expert residuals
shared matrix plus learned per-expert Givens views (Mirror)

development.selection_metric: mean held-out MSE pooled across methods and both teacher modes

training.router: none; signed coefficient code is deterministic from input signs and identical across methods

storage.authority: actual serialized full inference payload bytes
storage.serialization: torch.save state_dict plus deterministic config JSON

success_gate: In all three fresh aligned worlds, Mirror MSE <=1.10x independent full-expert mixture MSE and <=0.70x its serialized payload; it must beat hard tying, scalar amplitude, and rank-1 residual controls on MSE. Independent mode maps the private-parameter boundary.
failure_gate: Mirror misses the aligned MSE or byte gate in at least two fresh worlds, or a simpler control reaches Mirror MSE with equal or fewer serialized bytes. Independent-mode failure alone is a structural boundary, not overall failure.
boundaries: linear experts and synthetic signed coefficient regions only
all four experts are evaluated; no sparse routing claim
signed coefficients are supplied by deterministic input-sign rule, so this isolates expert functional composition rather than learned routing
